transcript.text: My Beko keeps stopping randomly in the middle of a wash with water still in it. Sometimes it's fine for a week, then it does it twice in a day. The model starts WTG I think. I've cleaned the filter. Driving me mad.

Since cleaning the filter hasn't fixed it, we need to narrow down whether the issue is drainage or sensing. To help me find the exact parts and checks for your machine, could you please provide the full model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I only know it starts WTG, the sticker inside the door is all faded and I haven't got the receipt either. Is there anything else you can work with? It's about 6 years old if that helps.

Yes, we can work with that. Even if the filter is clean, there could be debris (like a coin or hair) stuck in the drain pump impeller itself, preventing it from spinning fast enough to empty the tub. Alternatively, the pressure switch (which tells the machine how much water is inside) might be faulty or its small tube blocked. Please do this check: with the machine unplugged and a towel ready for water, open the small access flap at the bottom right (or remove the kickplate). Reach in to feel the pump impeller. Is it free to spin, or is something stuck? Also, when it stops mid-wash, does it make no noise at all, or do you hear a faint buzzing/humming from that area?

I've only ever opened the little filter flap, and I'm not taking the kickplate or any panels off, sorry. I couldn't feel the impeller through the filter hole either, I didn't try. Nothing odd noise-wise before it stops, no humming that I've noticed. The pump does sometimes run for a few seconds and then stops, if that means anything.

Thanks for clarifying. The fact that the pump runs briefly then stops, with no humming noise before it cuts out, suggests the pump motor itself is struggling—either because something (like a coin or hair) is jamming the impeller inside the housing, or the pump motor is failing electrically. Since you can't reach the model number right now, let's do two quick checks to confirm this. First, check the drain hose at the back of the machine: make sure it isn't kinked and that the end going into your waste pipe isn't blocked. Second, if your machine has a 'Drain' or 'Spin only' programme, try running it. Listen carefully: does the pump hum loudly for a few seconds then cut out (suggesting a blockage), or is it completely silent? This will tell us if we are looking at a simple hose issue or a faulty pump.

The drain hose is fine, it goes into a standpipe and isn't kinked, and the water drains out normally on a good wash. I haven't tried a drain or spin only programme and I wouldn't know what the pump should sound like to be honest. It's only when it stalls with water in the drum that it's a problem, so I can't really test it on demand.
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
Hello? I think your last message didn't come through, it just said the service was unavailable. Can you send it again?

Apologies for that interruption. The fact that it stops with water inside suggests the machine is waiting for the tub to empty before it can proceed. To rule out a simple blockage at the waste end, please pull the drain hose back slightly and check that the end going into your standpipe isn't pushed in too deep (which can cause it to suck shut) or blocked by debris. Also, ensure there is no kink in the hose where it bends against the wall. If the hose looks clear and un-kinked, but the problem persists, it is highly likely that the drain pump motor itself is failing intermittently. This often happens when a component inside the pump gets hot or worn out.

I already said the hose is fine and not kinked, it goes into a standpipe. I'll have a look at how far in it's pushed though. If it is the pump motor failing, what do I do about it? I'm not opening the machine up.

If the pump motor is indeed failing, it needs to be replaced by a qualified engineer because it involves removing the front panel and disconnecting water and electrical lines inside the machine. I would recommend calling out an appliance repair engineer to replace the drain pump for you.
